words.definition: Worth a lot of money or very useful.
words.example: Don't leave valuable items in the car.

words.definition: Very important or valuable to you.
words.example: Her photos are precious to her.

words.definition: Very rich or generous, often with too much spending.
words.example: They threw a lavish wedding for 300 guests.

words.definition: Having little money, or of low quality.
words.example: The service was poor.

words.definition: Having a lot of money, or containing a lot of something.
words.example: This chocolate cake is very rich.

words.definition: Treating people equally, or reasonable.
words.example: That sounds like a fair price.

words.definition: Of good enough quality.
words.example: We found a decent hotel near the station.

words.definition: Having a certain value, or deserving the effort.
words.example: This museum is worth a visit.

words.definition: Not mixed with anything else.
words.example: This bracelet is pure gold.

words.definition: Real or honest, not fake.
words.example: She seems like a genuine person.

words.definition: To look quickly at something.
words.example: She glanced at her watch.

words.definition: To look at something for a long time without moving your eyes.
words.example: It's rude to stare.

words.definition: To look quickly at something, often secretly.
words.example: Don't peek! It's a surprise.

words.definition: To close one eye quickly to send a friendly signal.
words.example: He winked at me across the room.

words.definition: To show something with your finger.
words.example: Don't point at people.

words.definition: To let someone see something.
words.example: Can you show me how it works?

words.definition: To make something known that was secret.
words.example: She refused to reveal the secret.

words.definition: To see or notice something.
words.example: I spotted my brother in the crowd.

words.definition: To come into sight, or to seem.
words.example: A message appeared on my screen.

words.definition: To put something where people can see it.
words.example: The shop displays its best shoes in the window.

words.definition: A small, smooth stone.
words.example: She picked up a pebble from the beach.

words.definition: A small pool of water on the ground.
words.example: Don't step in that puddle!

words.definition: Wet, soft earth.
words.example: My boots are covered in mud.

words.definition: Dry dirt in the form of a fine powder.
words.example: There's dust on the shelves.

words.definition: A cloud of very small drops of water close to the ground.
words.example: Mist covered the valley this morning.

words.definition: An area of wet, soft land.
words.example: Alligators live in the swamp.

words.definition: The regular rise and fall of the sea.
words.example: The tide is coming in.

words.definition: A surface that goes up or down at an angle.
words.example: We skied down the slope.

words.definition: A long, narrow area of high land.
words.example: We walked along the ridge.

words.definition: The hard material that trees are made of.
words.example: The table is made of oak wood.

words.definition: To pull something heavy along the ground.
words.example: We dragged the sofa into the living room.

words.definition: To move smoothly over a surface.
words.example: The kids slid down the hill on a sled.

words.definition: To push roughly.
words.example: Someone shoved me in the crowd.

words.definition: To throw something lightly.
words.example: Toss me the keys.

words.definition: To turn something over quickly.
words.example: Flip the pancake when it's golden.

words.definition: To turn something around, or to bend it into a curve.
words.example: Twist the lid to open the jar.

words.definition: To put something briefly into a liquid.
words.example: Dip the bread in the soup.

words.definition: To make a hole in the ground.
words.example: The dog dug a hole in the yard.

words.definition: To pick something up with a spoon or your hands.
words.example: Scoop the ice cream into bowls.

words.definition: To arrange things in a neat pile.
words.example: Stack the chairs against the wall.

words.definition: A group of things that are fastened or growing together.
words.example: He bought a bunch of bananas.

words.definition: A number of things on top of each other.
words.example: There's a pile of laundry on the bed.

words.definition: A large untidy pile.
words.example: The clothes lay in a heap on the floor.

words.definition: A group of things tied together.
words.example: He carried a bundle of newspapers.

words.definition: The amount you can hold in one hand, or a small number.
words.example: Add a handful of nuts.

words.definition: A large piece of something.
words.example: He cut the cheese into chunks.

words.definition: A small piece of something, such as paper or food.
words.example: I wrote his number on a scrap of paper.

words.definition: A very small piece of bread or cake.
words.example: There are crumbs all over the table.

words.definition: A group of birds or sheep.
words.example: A flock of birds flew overhead.

words.definition: A large group of animals, like cows or elephants.
words.example: A herd of cows blocked the road.

words.definition: To make your hair neat with a comb.
words.example: Comb your hair before school.

words.definition: To cut hair from your skin with a razor.
words.example: He shaves every morning.

words.definition: To cut a small amount off something to make it neat.
words.example: I need to trim my beard.

words.definition: To wash soap off with clean water.
words.example: Rinse your hair well.

words.definition: To clean by rubbing hard.
words.example: Scrub the pan with a brush.

words.definition: To rub something to make it shine.
words.example: He polished his shoes before the interview.

words.definition: To join cloth together with a needle and thread.
words.example: Can you sew this button back on?

words.definition: To put cream on your skin to stop it being dry.
words.example: Moisturize your skin after you shower.

words.definition: To change the color of something, such as hair or cloth.
words.example: She dyed her hair red.

words.definition: To wash yourself in a bath.
words.example: We bathe the baby every evening.

words.definition: A word that names a person, place or thing.
words.example: "Dog" is a noun.

words.definition: A word that shows an action or state.
words.example: "Run" is a verb.

words.definition: A word that describes a noun.
words.example: "Big" is an adjective.

words.definition: A word that describes a verb or adjective.
words.example: "Quickly" is an adverb.

words.definition: A word that replaces a noun, like "she" or "it".
words.example: Use a pronoun instead of repeating the name.

words.definition: A part of a sentence with a subject and a verb.
words.example: This sentence has two clauses.

words.definition: The form of a word that means more than one.
words.example: The plural of "child" is "children".

words.definition: The punctuation mark used to separate parts of a sentence.
words.example: You need a comma here.

words.definition: Marks like commas and periods used in writing.
words.example: Check your spelling and punctuation.

words.definition: A part of a word with one vowel sound.
words.example: "Water" has two syllables.

words.definition: An outdoor area where children play.
words.example: The kids are at the playground.

words.definition: A long board that two children ride up and down.
words.example: They played on the seesaw.

words.definition: A box filled with sand for children to play in.
words.example: The toddler played in the sandbox.

words.definition: A colored wax stick for drawing.
words.example: The kids drew with crayons.

words.definition: A small picture with glue on the back.
words.example: She put a sticker on her notebook.

words.definition: A hard candy on a stick.
words.example: He got a lollipop at the dentist.

words.definition: A rubber object that a baby sucks.
words.example: The baby threw her pacifier.

words.definition: A small chair on wheels for pushing a baby.
words.example: She pushed the stroller through the park.

words.definition: A toy that makes a noise when shaken.
words.example: The baby shook the rattle.

words.definition: A cloth put under a baby's chin during meals.
words.example: Put a bib on the baby.

words.definition: The direction toward the top of a map.
words.example: We drove north along the coast.

words.definition: The direction opposite to north.
words.example: Birds fly south for the winter.

words.definition: The direction where the sun rises.
words.example: The sun rises in the east.

words.definition: The direction where the sun sets.
words.example: California is on the west coast.

words.definition: A tool with a needle that shows which way is north.
words.example: We used a compass to find our way.

words.definition: The line in the distance where the sky meets the land or sea.
words.example: The sun sank below the horizon.

words.definition: An imaginary line around the middle of the earth.
words.example: The country lies on the equator.

words.definition: One of the two points at the top and bottom of the earth, or a long thin stick.
words.example: Penguins live near the South Pole.

words.definition: The distance north or south of the equator.
words.example: The two cities are at the same latitude.

words.definition: The distance east or west on the earth's surface.
words.example: Give me the latitude and longitude.

words.definition: What you think or believe about something.
words.example: In my opinion, the first movie was better.

words.definition: To think something is true without checking.
words.example: I assumed you knew about the meeting.

words.definition: To feel unsure about something.
words.example: I doubt he'll show up on time.

words.definition: To make someone believe something or agree to do something.
words.example: She convinced me to try the new gym.

words.definition: To disagree with something and try to stop it.
words.example: Many residents oppose the new parking rules.

words.definition: To say firmly that something must happen or is true.
words.example: I insist on paying for dinner.

words.definition: To say that something is true, often when you do not want to.
words.example: I admit I was wrong about the restaurant.

words.definition: To say that something is not true.
words.example: He denied taking the money.

words.definition: To say that something is true without proof.
words.example: She claims she never got the email.

words.definition: To agree with and help someone or something.
words.example: My parents fully support my plan to study abroad.
